supporting_observations.claim: Two network logon attempts for ben.carter failed with NTLM and bad-password status, from 192.0.2.45 at 13:41:55 and 13:43:20 UTC.
At 13:44:45 UTC, a network logon for ben.carter succeeded using Kerberos from the same IP address, 192.0.2.45.
The failed attempts followed by a successful logon could reflect either corrected credentials or unauthorized credential use; these records do not distinguish between them.

Explorer set ben.carter's ProxyEnable registry value to 0 on WS-BCARTER-01 at 13:39:30 UTC. This is temporally near the alerted logons, but does not establish who initiated the setting change or its purpose.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC because of a collection outage.
The authentication records identify 192.0.2.45 as the source address but do not identify the originating host or person.
claims_not_established: Whether 192.0.2.45 corresponds to an authorized device or an unauthorized source.
Whether the successful logon was initiated by ben.carter or an attacker using valid credentials.
Whether the proxy setting change was related to the authentication attempts.
Whether the failed attempts and subsequent success were part of one actor's activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Resolve 192.0.2.45 against address-allocation, endpoint, and network records for the alert window.
Collect source-host authentication and process telemetry, if the source can be identified.
Recover proxy records for the outage window if available and correlate them with WS-BCARTER-01.
Confirm with ben.carter whether the logons and proxy setting change were expected.
